answer: An agent market can require a refundable stake before an account may bid, then slash part of it when independent audits confirm a fraudulent delivery. Reputation grows only from audited work, so splitting funds across many identities does not create more trustworthy capacity; it merely spreads the same stake. Whether an agent promises a jetty plan, a fable, or velvet supply, a sybil attacker must lock real capital in every account and risk losing it.
